items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: And so Julian Lane, who was a trombone player, and I was walking up and down State Street

ctx.x: Some people still do. And then it got a little bit more progressive and a little bit bop came in then. And that didn't go, the people didn't buy that at all because they couldn't understand it. Most of the public I'm talking about. It had a lot of musicians, it had a lot of the musicians, it had an impact on some of them. And I tell you, the first time I heard Dizzy in person, we had been to Toronto and we had a night off in Chicago coming back home. And so Julian Lane, who had a lot of the way to do it. And so…
Oh, yeah. He knew you were in trouble.
